summary: Rahul Peter Das is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Maulana Azad College, Calcutta, Cologne, and Hamburg. He held research and teaching posts at Hamburg, Bonn, and Groningen (1981-1994), before becoming chair at Halle-Wittenberg in 1994.

Raimon Panikkar worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Barcelona, Bonn, Complutense University, Lateran University, Mysore, and Banaras Hindu University. He held positions at Harvard (~1966-1971) and UC Santa Barbara (~1987-2010).

Philosopher Raimond Gaita was educated at St Patrick's College, Melbourne High School, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Leeds. He held academic posts at King's College London (~1989-2011) and Australian Catholic University (~1999-2011).

Rajan Gurukkal is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Calicut. He served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (~1989-2008) and held a post at IISc Bengaluru.

Indologist Rajendra Chandra Hazra completed his doctorate under Sushil Kumar De. He served as Lecturer at Jagannath University (1931) and the University of Dhaka (1939-1949), and as Associate Professor of Smrti and Purana at Sanskrit College (1951-1972).

Rajendralal Mitra worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He was educated at Hindu School and the University of Calcutta, and served as president of the Asiatic Society around 1885.

Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Calcutta (~1907-1911), Presidency University, and Banaras Hindu University (~1928-1930).

Tibetologist Ralf Kramer studied under David P. Jackson at the University of Hamburg (~1992-1997) and at the University of London (~1997-2002). He served as Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Libraries (~2008-2021).

Ralph Abraham worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley (~1960-1962), Columbia University (~1962-1964), and UC Santa Cruz (attested 2009).

Indologist and linguist Ralph Lilley Turner studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1907-1912). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1920-1922) and served as Director of SOAS University of London (~1937-1957).

Indologist Ralph T. H. Griffith studied at The Queen's College and under Horace Hayman Wilson. He succeeded James R. Ballantyne and served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1883).

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma studied at Patna University and earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held posts at Bihar University (~1953-1961) and the Central Sanskrit Board (attested 1981).
Ram Mohan Roy worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded Presidency University, Kolkata in 1816 and founded the Brahmo Samaj.

Ram Niwas Pandey works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, completing doctoral research under Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Shankar Tripathi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989-1998).

Historian and Indologist Ram Sharan Sharma studied at Patna College, Patna University, and SOAS. He held posts at Patna College (~1946-1958), SOAS (~1953-1956), the University of Toronto (~1965-1966), and the University of Delhi (~1973-1985).
Linguist and Indologist Rama Nath Sharma served as Professor at the University of Rochester from ~1970 to 1976 and as Professor at the University of Hawaii from ~1976 to 2012.

Ramaprasad Chanda worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Dhaka Collegiate School, Dhaka College, and Scottish Church College. He worked at Rajshahi Collegiate School, Calcutta University, and the Indian Museum (1921-1931).
Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji studied at the University of Calcutta from ~1946 to 1953 and later held an academic post there.
Indologist Ramchandra B. Athavale served as Professor of Sanskrit at L. D. Arts College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith.
